intent: Hold the iteration-10 geometry unchanged: five sensors at y = 0.07 m, x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.16 by 0.14 m body, 0.6 kg. This is the final iteration, so the design raced here is also the design carried into the unseen-track evaluation. I am keeping the geometry that completes oval and s-bend 20 of 20 rather than adding an untested wheel_track change that cannot be checked. Expected: oval and s-bend hold at 20 of 20, and the slalom progress moves only as far as the kd change allows. Wheel_track 0.10 m is recorded as an untested hypothesis for the slalom, not as a change in this design.
learning: Across iterations 5 to 10, look-ahead (y 0.06 to 0.07 m), spread (line losses 0.6 to 1.1 per run) and the integral term (ki 0.4 to 0.7) have all flattened on the slalom. Its progress rose from about 0.30 to 0.33 with ki, then to 0.55 with kp 2.8 (iteration 10), while max_error has stayed at 0.063 m. If the kd change does not clear the slalom, the untested lever is wheel_track of about 0.10 m, which could not be tested in this final iteration. I would also expect the oval and s-bend completions to be the first things to watch on the unseen track.
rationale:
Iteration 10 (y = 0.07 m, x = ±0.024 m, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track) is the best race so far at 703.4, and the Integrator's controller changes have moved the score up without changing geometry. Oval and s-bend both complete 20 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.545 and max_error 0.0629 m. That is the best slalom progress yet, and it is just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line losses on the slalom are 1.1 per run, far below the 2-per-run trigger for widening the spread. The evidence therefore still points to reversal reaction rather than sensing or look-ahead.

I am holding the geometry this iteration, as the Integrator asked, so the kd 1.0 controller change is the only variable. I considered the wheel_track 0.10 m step their plan names for iteration 11. The evidence supports testing it: the slalom signature matches the trigger, and the trigger conditions are now met. But this is the final iteration, so no later race can read it against a clean baseline. A narrower track would change turn rate on the oval and s-bend, where completion is currently 20 of 20. An untested change there could cost the final unseen-track race, which is scored once, with no chance to check it. The safer choice for the final design is the geometry that completes both tracks reliably.

I took the Integrator's advice on the geometry. The Integrator's point on look-ahead stands: y = 0.07 m is saturated, so I am not moving it. The spread stays at ±0.024 m, because line losses are below the widening trigger. Mass (0.6 kg), body and sensor size are unchanged, because none of their triggers fires and body width cannot widen the off-track floor. I expect oval and s-bend to hold at 20 of 20, and I expect the slalom to move only with the kd change. I state no score outcome for the controller.
